- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.05) after a downtrend, model under-reacts; increase forecast by 1–1.5% to align with sentiment shift.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecasts are above 75, adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period (first 5 days) when sentiment is negative; reduce first 3 forecast points by 0.5–1.0%.
- If sentiment history includes multiple +0.20+ spikes, model often fails to correct; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.3% per +0.10 sentiment spike.
